title: Caption-then-embed vs multimodal embeddings vs page images
summary: Four ways to make visual content searchable: parse to text, caption figures with an LLM then embed the text, embed images directly into one vector, or embed whole pages as multi-vector images. The right one depends on where meaning lives, how users query and what evidence the answer must carry.
useIf: You are designing retrieval over documents or images with figures, and must choose the indexing path and how to evaluate it.
avoidIf: The corpus is plain text with no figures. A normal text index already does the job.

explain.md: Azure AI Search documents two image paths [[r12]]. **Verbalize** with the GenAI Prompt skill: one LLM call per image, which supports hybrid text queries and citations. **Embed directly** with the Azure Vision or AML skill: no LLM at index time, supports image-to-vector queries and look-alike search, but gives no reasons or citation text. For mixed corpora use both. A third idea skips parsing and embeds the page image itself as many vectors (ColPali family), with about 30 times the storage of a text vector per page [[r14]]. Mixed corpora often justify two paths side by side.

The Content Understanding skill adds cross-page tables, bounding polygons and semantic chunking, and its image descriptions need REST `2026-05-01-preview`. New skillsets should use it instead of the Document Layout skill (mixed GA and preview, checked 2026-10-13) [[r12]]. Pick by evidence form first: citable text, similarity, or page-level relevance. Then check storage and index-time cost, and keep retrieval scores separate from answer scores.

pitfalls.symptom: The right page is retrieved but the answer misquotes a chart
pitfalls.cause: Generation misread the figure, and retrieval was never measured on its own
pitfalls.fix: Evaluate retrieval and answers separately, and crop or raise image detail for the generator.

pitfalls.cause: The golden set is text only
pitfalls.fix: Stratify the golden set by modality and report each stratum.

scenarios.title: Manuals plus customer photos
scenarios.situation: A support assistant answers from product manuals and also lets customers upload a photo of a broken part to find similar parts and the matching manual page.
unknowns: How big is the parts photo library?
Is a GA-only rule in force?
scenarios.question: How do you index?

options.name: Two paths: verbalize or parse the manuals for text, and embed part photos for image queries
options.why: Mixed corpora often need both: citations for manuals and look-alike search for photos [[r12]].
options.tradeoff: Two pipelines and a result merge.

options.name: One path: caption every photo and manual figure
options.why: A single text index and simple merge.
options.tradeoff: Photo queries match only through descriptions.

options.name: One path: single-vector embeddings for everything

flips.then: Consider page images for those manuals.

scenarios.takeaway: Mixed corpora justify two indexing paths.

scenarios.title: Chart answers are wrong
scenarios.situation: A reporting assistant gives wrong chart values. The team proposes switching to a larger generator model before checking anything else.
unknowns: Does the generator read the chart correctly given the page?
scenarios.question: What do you do first?

options.name: Build a chart stratum in the golden set and measure retrieval and answer correctness separately
options.why: It tells you whether the miss is retrieval or generation before you spend on a fix.

options.name: Swap in a larger generator model
options.why: If the right page is never retrieved a bigger model cannot help, and chart reading stays a known weak spot.
options.tradeoff: Reasonable after measurement shows generation is the issue.

options.name: Re-index everything as page images
options.why: May fix retrieval of figure pages.
options.tradeoff: Large cost, and untested against the real cause.

flips.if: Retrieval recall on charts is high
flips.then: Fix generation: crop figures, raise detail, request data tables.

flips.if: Recall on chart pages is low

scenarios.takeaway: Measure retrieval and answers apart before changing paths.

quiz.q: A corpus has manuals needing citations and a photo library searched by example. Which design does the Azure AI Search guidance support?
quiz.explain: The guidance says to use both for mixed corpora: verbalization gives citations and hybrid queries, direct embedding gives image-to-vector queries. Either path alone fails one half of the corpus.

quiz.q: Match each indexing path with its main weakness.

pairs.r: About 30 times the storage per page

quiz.explain: Each path trades something: cost, explanation, storage or visual meaning.

quiz.q: Chart questions fail in production while the offline score is high. Which causes are plausible?
options: The golden set has no chart stratum
Retrieval and generation were never scored separately
Generators can misread graphs and line styles
quiz.explain: A text-only golden set, joint scoring and chart-reading limits all explain it. An odd embedding dimension would not produce this pattern.

flashcards.front: What are the two image paths in Azure AI Search multimodal search?
flashcards.back: Verbalize with the GenAI Prompt skill (one LLM call per image, citations and hybrid queries) or embed directly with the Azure Vision or AML skill (no LLM, image queries, no citation text). Use both for mixed corpora.

flashcards.front: Why evaluate retrieval separately from answers in multimodal RAG?
flashcards.back: A retrieval miss and a generator misread both produce wrong answers. Only separate scores show which to fix.

flashcards.front: Which Content Understanding skill detail needs a preview REST version?
flashcards.back: Image descriptions need REST `2026-05-01-preview`. The skill also gives cross-page tables, bounding polygons and semantic chunking.
